issues.title: Hardcoded RabbitMQ Host Configuration
issues.description: RabbitMQ host is hardcoded to 'localhost'. This prevents deployment to cloud environments without code changes.
issues.recommendation: Externalize configuration to environment variables or configuration files. Use Azure App Configuration or Key Vault for cloud deployments.
issues.suggestedFix: Read from environment variable: System.getenv("RABBITMQ_HOST") or use Spring configuration

issues.title: Hardcoded Queue Name
issues.description: Queue name is hardcoded. This limits flexibility and makes it difficult to use different queue names for different environments.
issues.recommendation: Externalize queue name to configuration. Consider using Azure Service Bus with Topics for more advanced routing.
issues.suggestedFix: Read from environment variable or configuration file

issues.title: Hardcoded RabbitMQ Host in Client
issues.description: RabbitMQ host is hardcoded in the client application, preventing cloud deployment.
issues.recommendation: Use environment variables or configuration files for host configuration.

issues.title: Outdated Java Version
issues.description: Project uses Java 1.8 which is outdated. Consider upgrading to Java 11, 17, or 21 LTS versions for better performance, security, and Azure compatibility.
issues.recommendation: Upgrade to Java 17 or Java 21 (LTS versions) for improved performance and security. Azure App Service fully supports these versions.

issues.title: Outdated Java Version in Client
issues.description: Client project uses Java 1.8. Upgrade recommended for better Azure integration.
issues.recommendation: Upgrade to Java 17 or Java 21 LTS for better performance and long-term support.

issues.title: Outdated Gson Version
issues.description: Gson version 2.8.9 is outdated. Latest version has security fixes and improvements.
issues.recommendation: Update to Gson 2.10.1 or later for security patches and performance improvements.

issues.title: Outdated JUnit Version
issues.description: JUnit 4.11 is very outdated. Consider upgrading to JUnit 5 for modern testing features.
issues.recommendation: Upgrade to JUnit 5 (Jupiter) for improved test capabilities and better IDE integration.

issues.title: RabbitMQ Can Be Replaced with Azure Service Bus
issues.description: Application uses RabbitMQ for messaging. Azure Service Bus provides a fully managed alternative with better cloud integration.
issues.recommendation: Consider migrating to Azure Service Bus for a fully managed messaging service with enterprise features. Azure Service Bus supports AMQP protocol and offers queues, topics, and advanced routing.
issues.suggestedFix: Replace with Azure Service Bus SDK: com.azure:azure-messaging-servicebus

recommendations.title: Externalize All Configuration
recommendations.description: Move all hardcoded configuration values (RabbitMQ host, queue names, ports) to external configuration sources.
benefits: Enables deployment to multiple environments without code changes
Improves security by separating secrets from code
steps: Create application.properties or application.yml configuration file
Use environment variables for sensitive values
Consider Azure App Configuration for centralized configuration
Use Azure Key Vault for secrets management

recommendations.title: Migrate to Azure Messaging Services
recommendations.description: Replace RabbitMQ with Azure Service Bus for a fully managed, scalable messaging solution.
benefits: Eliminates need to manage RabbitMQ infrastructure
Built-in high availability and disaster recovery
steps: Create Azure Service Bus namespace
Create queues and topics as needed
Update application to use Azure Service Bus SDK
Migrate message producers and consumers
Test thoroughly before production deployment

recommendations.title: Consider Azure SignalR Service for WebSocket
recommendations.description: Replace custom WebSocket implementation with Azure SignalR Service for better scalability.
benefits: No need to manage WebSocket infrastructure
steps: Create Azure SignalR Service resource
Integrate SignalR client library
Update application to use SignalR hubs
Configure connection management

recommendations.title: Upgrade to Java 17 or 21 LTS
recommendations.description: Upgrade from Java 8 to a current LTS version for improved performance, security, and support.
benefits: Long-term support from Oracle and Azure
Access to modern Java language features
steps: Update pom.xml compiler settings to Java 17 or 21
Test application compatibility
Update dependencies if needed
Update CI/CD pipelines
Update Azure App Service runtime configuration

recommendations.title: Update Dependencies to Latest Stable Versions
recommendations.description: Update Gson, JUnit, and other dependencies to latest stable versions.
steps: Review current dependency versions
Check for known vulnerabilities
Update to latest stable versions
Run tests to ensure compatibility

recommended.reasoning: Fully managed platform for hosting Java applications with built-in scaling, monitoring, and CI/CD integration
Fully managed enterprise messaging service with high reliability, security, and Azure integration
Managed real-time messaging service with automatic scaling and backplane support
Store and manage container images for deployment
Securely store connection strings, API keys, and other sensitive configuration
Monitor application performance, detect issues, and track usage

optional.purpose: Alternative to App Service for containerized deployment
optional.reasoning: Microservices-focused platform with built-in scaling and Dapr integration
Improve application performance with distributed caching
If exposing APIs to external consumers

migrationStrategies.name: Lift and Shift
migrationStrategies.approach: Minimal changes, deploy to Azure App Service with existing architecture
steps: Externalize configuration to environment variables
Deploy RabbitMQ as container or use managed service
Deploy WAR to Azure App Service
Update client to connect to Azure-hosted services

migrationStrategies.name: Refactor for Azure
migrationStrategies.approach: Modernize application to use Azure-native services
steps: Replace RabbitMQ with Azure Service Bus
Replace WebSocket with Azure SignalR Service
Externalize all configuration to Azure App Configuration
Store secrets in Azure Key Vault
Upgrade to Java 17
Deploy to Azure App Service with Application Insights
Implement CI/CD pipeline with Azure DevOps or GitHub Actions
cons: Team needs to learn Azure services

migrationStrategies.name: Containerize and Deploy
migrationStrategies.approach: Containerize applications and deploy to Azure Container Apps or AKS
steps: Create Dockerfiles for applications
Set up Azure Container Registry
Deploy to Azure Container Apps or AKS
Configure service communication
Implement monitoring and logging

notes: Costs are estimates and may vary based on region and usage
Service Bus charges include base + per-million-operations
Application Insights costs scale with data volume
Consider Reserved Instances for production workloads to save costs
